title: D2606039 DECISION DISMISSING PRO CLOUD SAAS, LLC’S REGISTRATION
text:
CD/RO1/KOL Date of Issuance: 06-23-2026
Decision D.26-06-039
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF
CALIFORNIA
Application of Pro Cloud SaaS, LLC for
Registration as a Telephone Corporation Application 25-11-013
pursuant to Public Utilities Code Section 1013.
DECISION DISMISSING PRO CLOUD SAAS, LLC’S REGISTRATION AS
A NON-FACILITIES BASED FIXED INTERCONNECTED VOIP
PROVIDER
On November 10, 2025, Pro Cloud SaaS, LLC (Pro Cloud) filed an
application for registration as a non-facilities-based fixed interconnected Voice
over Internet Protocol (VoIP) provider in California pursuant to the Provisions of
Public Utilities (Pub. Util.) Code Section 1013.1 No timely protests to the
application were filed.
Pro Cloud’s application was incomplete because it did not demonstrate a
minimum of $25,000 reasonably liquid and available to meet the firm’s first-year
expenses, including an additional $25,000 for deposits, which may be required by
local exchange carriers or interexchange carriers as a non-facilities-based fixed
interconnected VoIP provider. In addition, Pro Cloud did not sufficiently respond to
questions regarding the service territories where it plans to provide service, its future
service date, and its affiliated entity information. Furthermore, Pro Cloud failed to
use the most recent 1013 Registration Form.
1 Decision (D.) 97-06-017, as modified by D.10-19-017, D.11-09-026, and D.24-11-003.
609452500

A.25-11-013 CD/RO1/KOL
As a courtesy, Communications Division staff sent multiple Notices of
Application Deficiency via email to Pro Cloud to give Pro Cloud an opportunity
to correct the deficiencies in its application, from February 2026 through April
2026.2 To date, Pro Cloud’s application remains incomplete.
As provided in Decision (D.) 97-06-107, if a registration is “unacceptable or
incomplete, the registration form will be returned to the applicant for further
actions consistent with Commission rules and regulation.”3 Through this
decision, Pro Cloud’s registration is deemed returned. Accordingly, the
Commission dismisses Application 25-11-013 without prejudice.
Pro Cloud is eligible to reapply when it can meet the current requirements
for registration as a non-facilities-based fixed interconnected VoIP provider in
California pursuant to the provisions of Pub. Util. Code Section 1013. Pro Cloud
may also seek to operate in California by applying for a Certificate of Public
Convenience and Necessity pursuant to Pub. Util. Code Section 1001.4 This
proceeding is closed.
Findings of Fact
1. Application 25-11-013 was filed on November 10, 2025.
2. Pro Cloud failed to provide the requisite supporting financial
documentation to demonstrate a minimum of $25,000 reasonably liquid and
available to meet the firm’s first year expenses, including an additional $25,000
for deposits which may be required by local exchange carriers or interexchange
carriers as a non-facilities based fixed interconnected VoIP provider.
2 On February 3, 2026, Communication Division (CD) staff sent Pro Cloud a Notice of Application
Deficiency. On March 19, 2026, CD staff sent Pro Cloud another Notice of Application Deficiency.
3 D.97-06-107 at 9.
4 D.97-06-107 at Ordering Paragraph 8; D.10-09-017 at Conclusion of Law 12.
- 2 -

A.25-11-013 CD/RO1/KOL
3. Pro Cloud failed to sufficiently respond to questions related to the
service territories where it plans to provide service, its future service date, and
its affiliated entity information.
4. Pro Cloud failed to use the most recent 1013 Registration Form.
5. The application complied with all other requirements of the registration
process adopted in D.97-06-017, as modified by D.10-19-017,
D.11-09-026, and D.24-11-003.
6. No timely protests to the application were filed.
Conclusions of Law
1. It is consistent with the Commission’s rules and regulations for the
Executive Director to return Pro Cloud’s incomplete application by rejecting the
registration without prejudice.
2. Pro Cloud should be eligible to reapply when it is able to meet the
current requirements for registration as a non-facilities-based fixed
interconnected VoIP provider in California pursuant to the provisions of Pub.
Util. Code Section 1013.
3. Pro Cloud should be eligible to seek to operate in California by applying
for a CPCN pursuant to Pub. Util. Code Section 1001 if it is not eligible to
reapply for registration as a non-facilities based fixed interconnected VoIP
provider in California pursuant to the provisions of Pub. Util. Code Section
1013.
O R D E R
IT IS ORDERED that:
1. Pro Cloud SaaS, LLC’s application for a registration as a non-facilities
based fixed interconnected VoIP provider in California pursuant to the
Provisions of Public Utilities Code Section 1013 is dismissed without prejudice.
- 3 -

A.25-11-013 CD/RO1/KOL
2. Application 25-11-013 is closed.
Dated June 22, 2026, at San Francisco, CA.
